about: Real trends from 2-7 November 2026, collected 2026-11-07 for the 'live' mock in backend/app/trends.py. Each url is the article the facts come from. Order = best fit for Boabe first; get_trend(live=True) returns the first one.

trends.title: "Money can't buy you happiness": montages of small luxuries
trends.summary: A TikTok format listed among November's trends: creators post a montage of small luxuries, such as matching coffee cups, a new outfit, a holiday or a plated dessert, and end on a playful caption about cheesecake. The audio is "suara asli - Nadora | Cycling Journal".

trends.title: "Winter Arc": young Romanians start their New Year changes now, not on 1 January
trends.summary: A viral TikTok challenge picked up in Romania: instead of waiting for 1 January, people commit to becoming their best version before New Year's Eve. They go to the gym four to six times a week, cut chips and fast food, and read 10 to 20 pages a day instead of scrolling. A psychologist warns that a fast, radical change can lead to severe exhaustion.

trends.title: Early Christmas countdowns with cosy clips
trends.summary: Creators post cosy clips, such as hot cocoa, fireplaces and holiday movie nights, with text like "99 days until Christmas" and milestone updates, set to Christmas songs.

trends.title: "What I thought of this morning": summer memories in November
trends.summary: A nostalgia format on original audio: creators post summer memories, such as long lunches, golden-hour sunsets and sea dips, captioned with a version of "what I thought of this morning".

trends.title: A $105 cup of coffee in San Francisco loses a blind test to $5 drip
trends.summary: The Wild Fox, a Japanese-inspired cafe in San Francisco, went viral for a $105 cup made from a Brazilian Cup of Excellence lot (score 93.14) roasted in Tokyo by Glitch Coffee. In a CNN blind taste test the reporter found the $5 drip coffee "way more balanced". The cafe says the beans are grown for competition, not as commodities.

trends.title: "Fibermaxxing": people track how much fibre each meal has
trends.summary: On TikTok and Instagram, "fibermaxxing" encourages eating more fibre-rich foods, such as oats, chia seeds, lentils, beans, fruit and vegetables, sometimes tracking the fibre in every meal, with fibre-focused recipes, snacks and drinks.
